correctness.rationale: Independent reconstruction of all nine original lines and 36 cross-product pairs gives 6 double, 4 triple and 3 quadruple points. Blowing up the last seven yields 16 geometrically rational components and 30 transverse nodes, genus 15; each has at least 3 markings. The normalization units sequence identifies the torus character lattice with integral H1 of the 16-vertex 30-edge graph. The replayed standalone checker regenerates this graph and all 24 projective signed permutations, identifies all five conjugacy classes, computes the signed graph-action matrices on the 15-dimensional primitive fundamental-cycle basis, and verifies explicit determinant ±1 block transformations with 3 trivial+6 regular-2, 1 trivial+7 regular-2, 3 regular-4+1 regular-2+1 negative, 5 regular-3 for the nonidentity representatives. Every entry in the finite field rational-point and zeta table follows from these integral blocks, and the separate all-extension normalization formula uses the checked absence of edge reversals. Finite computation is an exhaustive certificate for these 24 integral identities, not a substitute for the separately written graph Picard and descent argument. Source files verify_b3_tori.py and verify_output.txt are embedded in this finding.

Geisser and Casalaina-Martin–Kass–Viviani provide general nodal Picard theory but not the explicit B3 lattice. The closest fully retrieved published arithmetic integral-torus findings concern Heawood and Igusa graphs, different objects and neither provides an implication to the five B3 forms. Actual published-finding corpus and literature queries compared aliases, genus, graph, integrality and normal forms. The claim passes best-knowledge originality with explicit historical priority risk; a failed literature search alone was not treated as proof.

value.rationale: The canonical resolved B3 Coxeter divisor is geometrically intrinsic to a classical reflection arrangement and yields a natural stable genus-fifteen degeneration. Its five finite-field Galois forms have five actual integral Picard tori, refining rational isogeny and abstract Frobenius eigenvalues; the order-four case reveals a norm-one factor requiring an integral, determinant-one certificate. The exhaustive S4 classification and all-extension zeta series are explicit usable arithmetic invariants of the degeneration. It is a complete classification for a motivated finite family, not a renamed generic Picard exact-sequence exercise, and is not subsumed by separately studied Heawood, Igusa, or Fermat-Ceva cases.
